artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth compact Riemannian three-manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$, for $s>\tfrac{n}{2}+1=\tfrac{5}{2}$. Equip $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with the right-invariant $L^2$ (kinetic energy) metric; its geodesics correspond, via the Arnold interpretation, to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Let $\exp_e: U \subset T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M) \to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ be the associated Riemannian exponential map at the identity.

It is known that, in contrast to the two-dimensional case, $\exp_e$ generally fails to be a nonlinear Fredholm map of index zero when $\dim M = 3$: there exist explicit initial velocity fields $v_0 \in T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ along whose geodesics the derivative $d\exp_e$ is not Fredholm.

Problem: Quantify this failure of the Fredholm property. For instance, for a geodesic with initial velocity $v_0$, determine the essential spectrum of the derivative $d\exp_e|_{tv_0}$ (viewed as a bounded operator on $T_e\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$), or otherwise provide a precise measure of its non-compactness. Specifically, decomposing $d\exp_e$ in the form $A + K_r$ where $A$ is an invertible operator and 
$$K_r w \;=\; (1-\Delta)^{-r/2}\, P_e\!\left(\iota_w\, d\,(1-\Delta)^{r/2} v_0^{\flat}\right)$$
(with $P_e$ the Hodge projection onto divergence-free fields, $\flat$ the metric musical isomorphism, and $r=0$ corresponding to the $L^2$ case), determine whether and how badly $K_0$ fails to be compact, and compute (or estimate) the essential spectrum of $d\exp_e$ along three-dimensional Euler geodesics.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature establishes that the L^2 exponential map on the volumorphism group is nonlinear Fredholm of index zero in dimension two but fails to be Fredholm in dimension three, with explicit non-Fredholm examples on three-manifolds (e.g., solid torus). A decomposition of the derivative into an invertible part plus a remainder K_r is available for H^r metrics with r>0, suggesting the L^2 failure is borderline, but no published work appears to quantify the failure (e.g., compute the essential spectrum) for compact Riemannian 3-manifolds. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Fredholm properties of Riemannian exponential maps on diffeomorphism groups
status_evidence.snippet: Exponential maps of right-invariant Sobolev H^r metrics on diffeomorphism groups are nonlinear Fredholm maps of index zero provided r is sufficiently large.
status_evidence.claim: Fredholm property holds for H^r with r large, motivating the question of borderline behavior at r=0 in 3D.

status_evidence.title: The Exponential Map of the Group of Area-Preserving Diffeomorphisms of a Surface with Boundary
status_evidence.snippet: The Riemannian exponential map of the right-invariant L2 metric on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of a 2D manifold with boundary is a nonlinear Fredholm map of index zero.
status_evidence.claim: Fredholm property holds in dimension two for the L^2 metric.

status_evidence.title: Normal Forms for the L2 Riemannian Exponential Map on Diffeomorphism Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the derivative of the L^2 exponential map and the operator K appearing in its decomposition; discusses explicit non-Fredholm examples in three dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit decomposition d exp = A + K used to discuss Fredholm failure in 3D.
